claims.text: The as-fabricated W–Cu composite has a random interfacial atomic structure between the tungsten and copper phases.
Sub-solidus thermal annealing can induce short-range atomic ordering at W–Cu interfaces.
Suitable annealing can produce interfacial SRO without causing phase coarsening or unwanted intermetallic formation.
Annealing at a sufficiently high temperature below melting or reaction temperatures provides the atomic mobility needed for interfacial ordering.
SRO formation can involve the development of ordered atomic clusters.
Thermal treatment will form ordered clusters or a more coherent interfacial layer specifically between tungsten and copper.
The ordered W–Cu interfacial structure will reduce interfacial lattice mismatch.
SRO reduces atomic displacements or vibrations.
Interfacial SRO in W–Cu will reduce phonon scattering at phase boundaries.
Reduced phase-boundary scattering will increase the phonon mean free path in the W–Cu composite.
Increasing SRO can increase lattice thermal conductivity relative to a random atomic arrangement.
A more ordered W–Cu interface will maintain mechanical load transfer by avoiding weak spots.
A more ordered W–Cu interface will preserve irradiation resistance by preventing weak spots or defect sinks.
The annealed W–Cu composite will have approximately 10–15% higher thermal conductivity than a conventionally processed W–Cu composite.
The annealed composite will retain mechanical strength comparable to the conventionally processed W–Cu composite.
The annealed composite will retain irradiation tolerance comparable to the conventionally processed W–Cu composite.
Excessively high annealing temperatures or prolonged treatment could cause grain growth or intermetallic formation.
Annealing-induced grain growth or intermetallic formation would compromise the composite's mechanical or irradiation properties.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant thermal-conductivity increase of about 10% or more, or observation of degraded mechanical or irradiation performance, will falsify the hypothesis.
